title: on_persistence_failure clears TX queue without _tx_lock and off the event loop
description: link_layer.py:2108 on_persistence_failure synchronizes on threading.RLock/Condition and is documented callable from any thread (persistence.py:262), yet calls tx_queue.clear() -> signal_all_pending(False) -> asyncio.Future.set_result, which is not thread-safe (lost wakeup/hang; RuntimeError under debug) and the queue mutation is not serialized against an in-flight drain holding _tx_lock. Failure interleaving: drain suspended in radio.transmit(E); persistence thread hits terminal failure -> clear() resolves E's reservation False; transmit completes on air -> complete(E, True) finds E removed, set_result(True) is idempotent first-wins -> send() returns False for a frame that was emitted -> upper layer retransmits -> duplicate frame on air. Outcome is timing-dependent (True may win if loop thread completes first). Fix: marshal the clear through loop.call_soon_threadsafe and acquire _tx_lock on the loop, or document/enforce loop-affinity for on_persistence_failure. Found by correctness+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.
